data_note: Snapshot scraped 2026-10-29T02:57:41Z, 21.3h old at analysis (GHA scrapes land ~09:40 BKK, after the 07:00 routine, so the freshest committed chain is always the prior session). Max-pain correction, and it reverses yesterday's note: scraper/scraper.py:968 IS inverted. _compute_max_pain accumulates call_oi*max(0, strike - settle) + put_oi*max(0, settle - strike), which pays calls off below the settlement candidate and puts off above it — both legs backwards. Recomputing the standard payoff over the committed chain gives max pain $4,250 today (total pain $9.09M) against the stored $5,300 (total pain $107.98M, an order of magnitude worse), and reproduces the inverted value exactly when the legs are flipped back. The same holds every session in the window: standard $4,300 / $4,265 / $4,260 / $4,250 / $4,250 versus stored $5,500 / $5,400 / $5,400 / $5,400 / $5,300. So the 10-27 note's '$4,260 corrected' figure was right and the 10-28 and 10-29 notes claiming the formula is sound were wrong. Treat the dashboard's Max Pain tile and history.json's max_pain series as inverted until the scraper is patched; real max pain is $4,250, only +$198 (+4.9%) above spot, which also explains why the stored value looks absurdly far away — 57.6% of call OI sits at strikes >= $4,900 and the inverted formula is dragged straight into that legacy block. Separately, history.json's gex_flip_strike (3,245 today) remains an artifact of build_history.py:77 breaking on the first cumulative sign change at the window's low edge; the durable flip, where cumulative net GEX crosses zero and stays positive, is $4,850.
